judgments.reason: The span 'an abnormally low transverse colon and right colic flexure, with small-bowel loops clustered above and to the right' appears literally in the CT findings and reflects abnormal bowel positioning consistent with malrotation, supporting the diagnosis. However, this finding alone is more indicative of malrotation than specifically midgut volvulus; it is a reasonable but incomplete support for the volvulus component of the completed label.

The span 'The third portion of the duodenum was not seen in its expected location' appears literally in the vignette and is a classic CT sign of intestinal malrotation (failure of normal duodenal fixation), clinically supporting the completed diagnosis of malrotation with midgut volvulus.

The span 'an abnormal superior mesenteric artery–vein relationship, with the vein coursing to the left of the artery' appears literally in the vignette and is a well-recognized CT sign of intestinal malrotation and midgut volvulus, directly supporting the completed diagnosis.

The span 'mesenteric congestion with prominent vessels' appears literally in the vignette and clinically supports midgut volvulus as a complication of malrotation, since mesenteric congestion reflects vascular compromise associated with volvulus.
